page_title: Vigil — stop being the message bus for your coding agents

summary.name: Vigil
summary.one_liner: A native macOS app that runs hierarchical trees of Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode agents, with manager and worker nodes that delegate work and report summaries upward.
use_cases: coordinate several coding agents on one task
split a large coding task across manager and worker agents
steer or interrupt a running coding agent
review full transcripts of finished agent runs
resume a Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode session
summary.what_it_does: Vigil shows a live tree of agent nodes: a root manager, sub-managers, and leaf workers, each with its own identity and scoped tools. Managers can recursively spawn other managers or workers, and communication follows the tree so context stays bounded. Each node hosts the real native TUI of Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, so users can open a worker, approve commands, steer plans, or interrupt it directly. Finished trees keep full node transcripts that can be replayed and resumed through each CLI's native session mechanism. The page says control is local with no hosted orchestration service.
notable: Hosts each agent CLI's real native TUI instead of a translated chat layer
Recursive delegation: managers can spawn sub-managers
Ground-truth transcript history with replay and resume per node
Local control with no hosted orchestration service
caveats: Requires at least one supported agent CLI installed (Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode)
Open source under GPL-3.0-or-later; pricing details not stated on the page
